name: claude-editorial-layout-system
description: A content-aware layout system that preserves one visual language while varying composition, geometry, density, and eye path across a deck.

archetypes.name: editorial-cover
archetypes.description: Large editorial title, one audience promise, and restrained metadata.
archetypes.avoid: Do not add an agenda, feature grid, and long subtitle to the cover.

archetypes.name: hero-statement
archetypes.description: One decisive claim with a compact proof rail or supporting number.
archetypes.avoid: Do not turn the proof rail into a dense dashboard.

archetypes.name: chapter-index
archetypes.description: A chapter opener that exposes the deck's next moves as an editorial index rather than a conventional agenda.
archetypes.avoid: Do not list every subtopic; keep three to five meaningful moves.

archetypes.name: asymmetric-editorial
archetypes.description: Offset copy and visual weight for a strong rhythm change without decorative novelty.
archetypes.avoid: Do not use asymmetry to hide weak hierarchy or random alignment.

archetypes.name: split-narrative
archetypes.description: Claim and explanation on one side, evidence or visual on the other.
archetypes.avoid: Do not default to a split layout when the content can use a more specific diagram or evidence pattern.

archetypes.name: metric-spotlight
archetypes.description: One dominant number supported by two or three smaller contextual measures.
archetypes.avoid: Do not enlarge a number that lacks a definition, source, or decision implication.

archetypes.name: evidence-claim
archetypes.description: A chart, screenshot, quotation, or source artifact anchored next to the conclusion it proves.
archetypes.avoid: Do not make the chart and conclusion compete at equal visual weight.

archetypes.name: annotated-visual
archetypes.description: One screenshot, architecture view, or product surface with two to four numbered callouts that explain why it matters.
archetypes.avoid: Do not cover the artifact with labels or use more than four callouts.

archetypes.name: quote-evidence
archetypes.description: A short quotation or customer statement paired with source context and one interpretation.
archetypes.avoid: Do not use anonymous, fabricated, or paragraph-length quotations.

archetypes.name: infographic-story
archetypes.description: A one-glance problem, method, and result narrative with a clear visual handoff.
archetypes.avoid: Do not reduce the story to three identical cards labelled problem, method, and result.

archetypes.name: data-journey
archetypes.description: A dominant metric connected to a simple trend so the audience sees both state and movement.
archetypes.avoid: Do not show a trend without definitions, time range, and a decision implication.

archetypes.name: dashboard-story
archetypes.description: A dashboard-like outcome surface where one state, one progress signal, and one next action dominate.
archetypes.eyePath: status to progress to next action
archetypes.avoid: Do not recreate a dense BI dashboard with equal-weight widgets.

archetypes.name: layered-architecture
archetypes.description: Stacked system layers with ownership, trust, or operational boundaries.
archetypes.avoid: Do not draw layers that do not change responsibility or policy.

archetypes.name: flow-architecture
archetypes.description: Directional nodes with direct labels for protocols, data, decisions, and ownership.
archetypes.avoid: Do not use unlabeled arrows or more nodes than can be read from the back of the room.

archetypes.name: system-map
archetypes.description: A central service or agent surrounded by actors, tools, context, and observability within explicit trust boundaries.
archetypes.eyePath: outside actors to central hub to boundary
archetypes.avoid: Do not create a logo cloud; every connection must explain access, data, or responsibility.

archetypes.name: architecture-boundary
archetypes.description: Control and data planes arranged around an explicit trust, network, or tenancy boundary.
archetypes.avoid: Do not draw a boundary without naming what crosses it and what enforces it.

archetypes.name: before-after
archetypes.description: Matched current and target states with one explicit delta between them.
archetypes.avoid: Do not compare unrelated criteria on the two sides.

archetypes.name: comparison-matrix
archetypes.description: Options evaluated on a shared axis with a clearly justified recommendation.
archetypes.avoid: Do not highlight the recommendation before the comparison is fair.

archetypes.name: decision-path
archetypes.description: A signal moves through an evaluation point into an explicit proceed or pause recommendation.
archetypes.avoid: Do not show branches without named criteria and owners.

archetypes.name: decision
archetypes.description: A small set of choices, the recommendation, and the consequence of waiting.
archetypes.eyePath: recommendation to alternatives to cost of waiting
archetypes.avoid: Do not end with a menu of options and no explicit ask.

archetypes.name: timeline
archetypes.description: Three to six milestones on a shared spine with the current phase made explicit.
archetypes.avoid: Do not use milestones that merely repeat dates without capability change.

archetypes.name: roadmap-horizon
archetypes.description: Now, next, and later milestones arranged on a horizon or perspective path to emphasize changing capability.
archetypes.avoid: Do not pretend that distant work has the same certainty as near-term work.

archetypes.name: process-steps
archetypes.description: Ordered stages where each step changes responsibility, state, or evidence.
archetypes.avoid: Do not turn every noun into a step; show state or responsibility change.

archetypes.name: swimlane-process
archetypes.description: A process distributed across actors or teams, with handoffs, approvals, and failure points made explicit.
archetypes.avoid: Do not omit the owner or trigger at a lane crossing.

archetypes.name: operating-loop
archetypes.description: A closed observe, decide, act, and learn loop organized around one outcome, cadence, and guardrail.
archetypes.avoid: Do not draw a loop when feedback does not materially change the next cycle.

archetypes.name: code-walkthrough
archetypes.description: Short projection-safe code or commands paired with the outcome they demonstrate.
archetypes.avoid: Do not use code as decoration or show more lines than the audience can read.

archetypes.name: risk-matrix
archetypes.description: Probability and impact combined with named mitigations and owners.
archetypes.avoid: Do not classify risks without a mitigation, owner, and review point.

archetypes.name: closing-manifesto
archetypes.description: A memorable final line and one concrete next action, usually with a strong rhythm break.
archetypes.avoid: Do not add a summary grid after the final ask.
